ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Mahalia Jackson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Cardiac MRI and FDG-PET results: cardiac sarcoidosis; start of prednisone and methotrexate, bone and infection protection, and electrophysiology referral

text.paragraph: Cardiac test results and the start of treatment. [S]

Ms. Jackson returns two weeks after the consultation with the results of her heart and eye tests. The Holter recorded first-degree atrioventricular block throughout, ectopic beats making up 6 percent of all beats, and three short runs of ventricular tachycardia, one during her palpitations. The echocardiogram and cardiac MRI show a mildly reduced pumping function (ejection fraction 47 percent) with scarring in the base of the septum and the side wall, and the FDG-PET three days ago shows active inflammation at the same sites. The eye examination was normal. Hepatitis B and C tests were negative, and she is not immune to hepatitis B. Cultures from the EBUS samples show no growth at three weeks. She is breathless on one flight of stairs, has had two more spells of palpitations, and has not fainted. She saw Dr. Asante-Miller and the cardiology team this morning. She asked whether she will sing again and was told that, with treatment, most people return to their work. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1964-03-09; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 91.2 kg; blood pressure 124/78, pulse 80 with occasional ectopic beats
Occasional ectopic beats; no murmur, gallop or ankle swelling; jugular venous pressure normal
No thrush; teeth in good repair
Thoughtful; asks about her voice and travel

Breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough for three months, worse on tour, with tiredness and chest tightness; she can no longer hold long phrases; bilateral hilar lymph node enlargement on today's chest radiograph; granulomas were reported at an abdominal operation twelve years ago, with no pathology report available: sarcoidosis must be confirmed by tissue and other causes excluded
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented breathlessness during performances and the 1952 granulomas. Superseded by the tissue diagnosis at the consultation.

Palpitations with two spells of light-headedness while singing; ECG today: sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR 240 ms) and frequent ventricular ectopic beats: cardiac involvement must be looked for
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when cardiac sarcoidosis was diagnosed.
Hypercalcemia: calcium 10.8 mg/dL with a high 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D and a low 25-hydroxyvitamin D, while taking an over-the-counter calcium and vitamin D supplement; creatinine slightly raised
S — Synthetic finding; resolved on treatment.

Pulmonary sarcoidosis with hilar and mediastinal lymph node involvement (Scadding stage II), confirmed by non-necrotizing granulomas on EBUS-guided lymph node aspiration with negative stains and cultures; mild restriction and reduced diffusing capacity; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented sarcoidosis
S — Synthetic histology, stage and lung function; her biographer reports a diagnosis of sarcoidosis after granulomas were found at an operation (D, probable).

Cardiac sarcoidosis: first-degree atrioventricular block, ventricular ectopy (6 percent of beats) with nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, left ventricular ejection fraction 47 percent, patchy late gadolinium enhancement of the basal septum and inferolateral wall, and matching focal FDG uptake on PET; synthetic modern detail linked to the documented private account that sarcoidosis was in her heart
S — Synthetic cardiac findings; the account that her doctors told her sarcoidosis was in her heart rests on her biographer (D, probable), and the interpretation of her later heart disease is R.
Long-term systemic glucocorticoid treatment for sarcoidosis, with bone, glucose, blood pressure, infection and eye risks to manage

list.item:
Cardiac sarcoidosis (D86.85). Cardiac sarcoidosis by the HRS criteria: sarcoidosis proven in lymph nodes, with unexplained first-degree atrioventricular block, nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, scar on MRI, matching active inflammation on PET and an ejection fraction of 47 percent. Active cardiac inflammation is treated with glucocorticoids and a steroid-sparing agent. The ejection fraction is above 35 percent, but the scar and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia make an electrophysiology study the next step to decide whether she needs a defibrillator. Dr. Asante-Miller and cardiology agree. [S]
Prednisone 40 mg each morning, with a taper planned over about six months.
Methotrexate 15 mg once weekly with folic acid 1 mg daily, increasing to 20 mg if tolerated.
Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily.
Electrophysiology study next week, with a dual-chamber defibrillator if sustained ventricular tachycardia is induced.
Repeat FDG-PET after about five months of treatment.

Pulmonary sarcoidosis with lymph node involvement (D86.2). The same treatment covers the lungs, where function is impaired and she has symptoms. [S]
Repeat lung function in about two months.

Long-term systemic glucocorticoid treatment (Z79.52). She will take prednisone for many months, with prediabetes (A1c 5.9%) and high calcium. Bone protection without calcium tablets while calcium is high; pneumocystis prophylaxis while prednisone is 20 mg or more with methotrexate, using atovaquone because trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole adds to methotrexate's effect on the marrow; vaccines today, before immunosuppression takes hold. [S]
Bone density scan next week, then alendronate 70 mg weekly.
Atovaquone 1500 mg daily.
PCV20, the first recombinant zoster dose and the first hepatitis B dose today.
Home glucose checks twice a week; no alcohol on methotrexate.

Hypercalcemia (E83.52). Calcium 10.6 mg/dL; expected to fall on prednisone. [S]
Calcium at the next visit.

Palpitations with conduction disease (R00.2). Explained by cardiac sarcoidosis, diagnosed today; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.

Follow-up: Bone density next week; electrophysiology study next week. No driving for a week after any device implant. Nine-week review with lung function and blood tests. Call 911 for fainting, a sustained racing heart or a defibrillator shock. Next scheduled visit 1964-05-11: nine weeks of treatment: lung function, calcium, methotrexate safety, the new defibrillator, steroid effects, and her concert schedule. [S]
